notes: Prompts mix triggering tests (would a real CodeLens phrasing pull this skill?) and output-quality tests (does the output follow the locked Java 21 conventions: virtual threads, records, sealed adapter, exhaustive switch, no preview APIs). Assertions are objectively checkable.

evals.prompt: In the CodeLens backend, write the component that reviews every diff chunk of a PR concurrently. One chunk failing (a timeout or bad LLM output) must not lose the comments from the other chunks.
evals.expected_output: A service using Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor(), submitting one task per chunk, joining each Future with a per-future try/catch so failures are isolated. No fixed-size pool, no preview APIs.

assertions.text: Uses Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()
Catches per-future exceptions so one chunk failure does not abort the others
Does NOT use a fixed-size thread pool (newFixedThreadPool / Executors.newFixedThreadPool)
Does NOT use StructuredTaskScope or any --enable-preview API

evals.prompt: Define the data types the review pipeline streams: the per-token fragment pushed over WebSocket and the completed, validated comment. Severity is critical/warning/suggestion.
evals.expected_output: Java records (not POJOs) for the token and comment, a Severity enum, and a compact constructor validating confidence in [0,1].

assertions.text: Declares the DTOs as record types, not classes with getters/setters
Defines an enum Severity with CRITICAL, WARNING, SUGGESTION
Validates confidence range in a compact constructor

evals.prompt: Set up the LLM provider in CodeLens so we can switch between a GPT-5 provider and a Claude provider without recompiling, and so the compiler forces us to handle every provider in any dispatch logic.
evals.expected_output: A sealed interface LlmReviewProvider permitting the concrete providers, with providerId(), reviewModel(), summarize(...) and Flux<ReviewEvent> streamReview(...) where ReviewEvent is a sealed Reset/Finding/Usage hierarchy; selection driven by config; exhaustive switches with no default.

assertions.text: Declares a sealed interface with a permits clause listing the providers
Provider is selected from configuration, not hardcoded in a service
Uses an exhaustive switch over the sealed type with no default branch
Streams a sealed ReviewEvent type (Reset / Finding / Usage), not raw strings or a single token record

evals.prompt: Add the helper that turns a review comment's severity into a labeled, emoji-prefixed string for the GitHub summary.
evals.expected_output: A switch pattern-matching expression over the Severity enum, exhaustive (no default needed).

assertions.text: Uses a switch expression over Severity
Switch is exhaustive over the enum constants with no default branch

evals.prompt: Write an integration test proving CodeLens cannot create two review sessions for the same PR and the same commit SHA.
evals.expected_output: A TestContainers test using pgvector/pgvector:pg16-alpine wired via @DynamicPropertySource, asserting the second save of the same (pr_id, head_sha) throws DataIntegrityViolationException.

assertions.text: Uses Testcontainers with a real PostgreSQL image (pgvector/pgvector:pg16 compatible with postgres), not an embedded/in-memory database
Wires the container via @DynamicPropertySource
Asserts a DataIntegrityViolationException (or constraint violation) on the duplicate (pr_id, head_sha)
Does not silently skip when Docker is missing in CI (fails when CODELENS_REQUIRE_DOCKER=true)

evals.prompt: For the repo-aware context feature, gather a diff chunk's callers, its tests and similar code from the index in parallel; if any of them fails, the context for that chunk is incomplete.
evals.expected_output: Virtual-thread executor with three Futures; on failure of any, cancel(true) the others and throw. Explicitly NOT StructuredTaskScope (preview).

assertions.text: Runs the three lookups on a virtual-thread executor
On any failure, cancels the sibling futures before throwing (fail-together)
Does NOT use StructuredTaskScope
Builds ReviewPromptContext with all five components (chunk, callers, tests, systemContext, related)

evals.prompt: The Anthropic SDK gives me a blocking iterator of stream events. Turn it into a Reactor Flux for the CodeLens review pipeline so cancelling the Flux stops the HTTP stream.
evals.expected_output: Flux.create with the blocking loop on a virtual thread (Thread.ofVirtual), sink.next per parsed finding, complete/error at the end, a single onDispose hook that closes the stream response and interrupts the worker, checks of sink.isCancelled() in the loop.

assertions.text: Runs the blocking iteration on a virtual thread, not on the subscriber's thread or a fixed pool
Registers exactly one onDispose callback that closes the stream and interrupts the worker
Stops iterating when the sink is cancelled
Signals errors via sink.error and completion via sink.complete

evals.prompt: A retry of the provider stream sometimes duplicates findings in CodeLens because the first attempt had already emitted some. Fix the event model.
evals.expected_output: A Reset variant in the sealed ReviewEvent emitted at the start of every (re)subscription and when a fallback takes over; the consumer's exhaustive switch clears the chunk's findings on Reset and dedups by fingerprint.

assertions.text: Adds a Reset event to the sealed event type rather than tracking retries ad hoc
Emits Reset at the start of each subscription so retries begin from a clean slate
The consumer handles Reset in an exhaustive switch without a default branch
